findings.claim: Notifications are late because the outbox drains slower than it fills: 2880 arrivals vs 1980 publications in 900 s.
findings.reason: Pending grew 12 to 912 (the 900 gap) and the oldest undelivered age grew 0.8 s to 410 s, matching minutes-late reports.

findings.claim: Delivery throughput of ~2.2/s matches one poller delivering serially at ~452 ms per attempt.
findings.reason: 1/0.452 s is about 2.2/s, equal to 1980/900. Config shows one poller; batch 20 per 1 s poll would allow far more if deliveries were parallel.

findings.claim: No errors or request-path problem; per-delivery time is dominated by the consumer handler (~401 ms of ~452 ms).
findings.reason: All 201s at p95 0.24 s, 1980 SUCCESS records with no errors, failed 0, handler_ms p50 401, auth 51, unattributed 1.2.

alternatives.hypothesis: Slow consumer handler (~400 ms) is the root cause rather than poller design.
alternatives.reason: Handler time dominates attempt time, but the consumer is a fixture, so this may not reflect production.

alternatives.hypothesis: Delivery failures or retries are causing the delay.

raw_arguments.summary: The outbox backlog grew by 900 because the single poller published about 2.2/s against about 3.2/s arrivals. Oldest undelivered age reached 410 s. Deliveries are healthy but slow enough to cap throughput.

findings.claim: Publication throughput (~2.2/s) is below arrival rate (~3.2/s), so the outbox backlog grew by 900 and oldest age reached 410 s.
findings.reason: 2880 arrivals minus 1980 publications equals 900, matching the pending gauge rise 12->912; oldest undelivered age rose 0.8->410 s.

findings.claim: Delivery is not failing: all 1980 attempts succeeded with total_ms p95 470 and no errors; the request path is also healthy.
findings.reason: All SUCCESS, no network/server errors, tight latency; transfers requests all 201 with p95 0.24 s and no restarts.

findings.claim: The throughput cap likely comes from one poller with batch 20 and 1 s interval delivering serially at ~450 ms each (~2/s), matching the observed rate.
findings.reason: 20 deliveries x ~452 ms is ~9 s plus a 1 s poll interval, giving about 2/s, close to 2.2/s. Serial delivery is not directly observed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer handler slowness (~401 ms) is the real bottleneck rather than poller configuration.
alternatives.reason: Handler time dominates per-attempt latency, but the fixture consumer may not reflect production, and the two causes interact.

alternatives.hypothesis: Transfer request failures or slow request handling delayed enqueueing.
alternatives.reason: Requests were all 201 with a low p95, and arrivals were committed (2880) in the window, so the delay is after commit.

limitations: Whether the poller delivers serially or concurrently is not directly observed; the capacity explanation is inferred from arithmetic.
Only a 15-minute window and a fixture consumer were observed; no pre-window baseline shows when the backlog began.
next_checks: Inspect poller code or traces to confirm serial versus concurrent delivery within a batch.
Test a larger batch, shorter interval, or concurrent delivery in staging and watch whether the pending gauge drains.

raw_arguments.summary: Outbox delivery throughput (~2.2/s) is below arrival rate (3.2/s), so the backlog grew by 900 and the oldest undelivered age reached 410 s. Likely cause is a single sequential poller bound by ~450 ms per delivery.

findings.claim: Delay is queueing in the outbox, not failures or slow request handling.
findings.reason: Failed 0, all deliveries SUCCESS with no errors, transfers requests all 201 with p95 0.24 s and no restarts.

findings.claim: The ~2.2/s ceiling is consistent with one poller delivering sequentially at ~452 ms each (20 x 0.452 = ~9 s per batch).
findings.reason: Per-delivery total_ms p50 452 with one poller and batch 20 gives ~2.2/s, matching observed 1980/900 s; sequential delivery is not directly confirmed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer handler latency (~401 ms) is the real bottleneck rather than poller design.
alternatives.reason: Handler_ms dominates total time, but the consumer is a fixture so production latency is unknown.

alternatives.hypothesis: Delivery failures or retries cause the delay.
alternatives.reason: Zero failed and all 1980 attempts succeeded; no errors found.

limitations: Consumer is a fixture, so the ~450 ms per-delivery latency may not match production.
